findings.quote: gives a negative net force of size 3.66mg
findings.note: Kinetic friction at 30° is μmg cos30° = 0.866mg against a weight component of 0.5mg, so the net force is −0.366mg, of size 0.366mg. 3.66 is the acceleration in m/s² for the 60° case, not a force in units of mg; the stated cause cannot produce 3.66mg.
findings.fix: gives a negative net force of size 0.366mg (an acceleration of 3.66 m/s² up the incline with g = 10 m/s²), showing the block cannot actually be sliding there.

notes: Question does not fix g; the solution states g = 10 for the one numeric acceleration. The kinetic case takes μ_k = μ_s = 1, the standard reading when only the angle of repose is given.
